conjecture: Q104: is the hyperbola ts=1 the fixed-point set of an involution on the ribbon operators R_e(t)? (and Q107, its gating computation)

tree.approach: decide Q104 by first settling Q107 (is the Garsia-Zabrocki exponent c(R,mu)=n(mu u R)-n(mu) constant in mu?), then either build the involution or refute the framing

children.approach: Q107 settled in closed form: c(R,mu) = (r-1)e + maj(R), r = topmost row of the strip. Proof by double-counting descents against cell rows. Answer is (b): level sets are the fibres of r. Verified 1422 pairs, e=3,4,5, |mu|<=9, 0 mismatches; all 28 shapes non-constant.

Located the pin that makes Garsia-Zabrocki Thm 2.3 work: their step 'using 2.10' is n(mu+1^k)-n(mu)=binom(k,2), constant because mu+1^k adds cells at rows 1..k FIXED INDEPENDENTLY OF mu. Not because 1^k is a column: the same column ribbon added at r>=2 has c in {6,9,12,...}. Read at source, /tmp/browse/gz199/paper.tex ll.900-975.

DEAD END for the framing as posed: there is no scalar c with Theta R_e(t) Theta = t^c R_e(1/t) arising from the GZ mechanism, because the emitted exponent varies with the matrix element (Corollary of q107-closed-form).
children.reason: the Garsia-Zabrocki exponent c(R,mu)=(r-1)e+maj(R) is non-constant in mu for EVERY ribbon shape, e>=1, including columns; so the conjugation is not an operator identity with a scalar

children.approach: Q104 ANSWERED in corrected form: omega R_e(t) omega = t^(e-1) R_e(1/t), omega the standard involution s_lambda -> s_lambda'. Forced by ht(R)+ht(R^T)=e-1, itself from rows+cols=e+1 for a border strip. Verified as a matrix identity e=1..5, N=0..8 on a code-disjoint engine; transpose lemma 2670 pairs, 0 failures.

ts=1 IS a fixed-point set: of sigma(t,s)=(1/s,1/t) on the parameter torus, implemented on operators by Ad(omega) composed with the swap of the two commutator slots. On ts=1, Ad(omega) C_{e,e} = -C_{e,e}. Verified e=2,3,4, N<=3.

Two-bead sector of [R_e(t),R_f(s)] vanishes on ts=1 for ALL e,f>=1. Mechanism local on the Maya diagram: reversing the order of two disjoint bead moves shifts the e-height by -k and the f-height by +k, so the WEIGHT RATIO is (ts)^k, equal to 1 exactly on ts=1. At e=f the element factors as (1-(ts)^k)(t^{P-k}s^Q - t^Q s^{P-k}) -- the two exceptional loci ts=1 and s=t are the two factors. 30349 move-pairs, 0 failures.

HONEST NEGATIVE, and it is the load-bearing one: hyperbola-is-fix-sigma does NOT imply two-bead-vanishing. The one-bead sector satisfies the same eigenvalue equation on ts=1 and is NONZERO there (52/52 entries survive vs 0/58 two-bead). So the programme's hope that all four sightings of ts=1 become corollaries of one Z/2 is FALSE: two do, two do not. The one-bead order-of-vanishing results (Q105 Thms A,B) remain unexplained.
